newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover up in week to March 28.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover up in week to March 28.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) reported on Monday a 39.5 percent increase in its turnover during the week ending March 28 on an improved liquidity of banks and renewed trade in the central bank bonds.
Total BSE turnover rose to 59.404 million dinars ($10.68 million) in 206 deals, from 42.58 million dinars in 215 transactions.
"Improved liquidity of the banking sector immediately reflected on the bourse activity and there was definitely more money coming to the market," a trader told Reuters.
BSE spokesman Milko Stimac said the bourse turnover jumped mainly on higher trade in the central bank bonds.

There was no auction of the National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) short-term bonds, but the central bank offered last week three new tranches of 20-day bonds totalling 50 million dinars, keeping the rate unchanged at an annual 58.69 percent.
Two tranches worth 20 million dinars each were placed on the BSE and the third one worth 10 million dinars was offered via the Montenegro bourse.
NBY sold 26.7 million dinars worth of bonds on the BSE and another 0.3 million on the Podgorica-based Montenegro bourse.
Traders said NBY cut down maturity to 20 from 30 days to have all tranches expiring April 13.

"This was no ordinary offer of the NBY bonds and there was no previous announcement. It resembles a chain-like repayment of debt, first between companies and banks and then between banks and the central bank. And the debt is simply not called by its name," a trader said.
Apart from the NBY bonds, the BSE saw a growing activity in commercial paper and wheat contracts.
"Commercial paper attracted more investor interest ahead of a long weekend with banks and companies closed for a public holiday," Stimac said.
For the week ending March 28, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper traded 183 times for a volume of 27.931 million dinars.
* Treasury bills accounted for 11 deals worth 0.94 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between an annual 331 and 520 percent, while maturity stood between five and 30 days.
* The BSE reported six deals in the central bank short-term bonds totalling 26.7 million dinars.
* There were six transactions in wheat contracts worth 3.833 million dinars.
* Over-the-counter trade in commercial paper and treasury bills rose to 25.788 million dinars from 24.188 million a week ago.
* OTC trade in giro money, with banks trading surplus liquidity, jumped to 20 million dinars from 13.97 million a week ago. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
($1 = 5.5579 Yugoslav dinars)
